RUNC3RN YOU Nii MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION PICNIC. The annual picasic in connection with the Blitteo,lll Young Men's Christian Association took Place -11 Saturday last. So successful was the trip to Weaverhar° Wood last year that the committee decided to give tbs members an opportunity of again visiting that charring" spot; but we regret to say few were the members wheel love of natural scenery was strong enough to induce the.: to face the downfall of rain which threatened e're'-' moment to take place* as the time for starting —tero o'cloole —approached, for when the boat, drawn by a Weston Point steam tug, kindly lent by Captain Clark, drew aeraY from the lock on the Weaver Canal, Weston Point, shortly after that hour, there were not more than 50 persons on board, and more than half of those were ladies. All dread of a discomforting wetting was provided against by a tarpsoli° which covered the boat, but its protection was unnecessari during the afternoon. Dark clouds disappeared to give place to others of etherial whiteness, while the sun 511503 with a power and a brightness heightened by the ereect of the previous gloom. Under such cirinstances the ever varying landscape—now a tie stretch of meadow land, whose monotony Was relieved here and there with clumps el trees and trim homesteads, Frodsharn hills rearing up their head boldly boldly behind, sheltering, as it were, the village below —now the boat slowly glides between trees rich with foliage, hiding the view beyond, when a gipsy, moving along tbe sloping bank, enveloped in a red cloak, invests the scene with a picturesqueness indescribable—now the undulating surface of the ground, glorying in verdure of the brightest green, and trees of noble build, formed glades where fancf easily behold Oberon and Titania holding their court in the moonlight hatching vexing vagaries—possessed a freshness seldom experienced, and tie time pissed pleasantly until the boat was moored at Weaverham Quay about halt-past four. The party at once proceeded to the farm cef Mr. Sanderson, where tea was partaken of. Under a etc' at the border of the orchard, the tea table °adorned with beautiful boquets of flowers, had been erected, and here the party was reinforced by the preeence of ad number of gentlemen who had arrived by train. The gee tea was thoroughly enjoyed, fresh zest being imparted to it by the novel conditions under which it was partaken, a tull2_ of the head bringing into view as pretty an English Jana; 'cape as could possibly be imagined. At the conclusion 0' the repast the Rev. J. Nowell proposed a vote of thanks to Mr. and Mrs. Sanderson for the excelleat manner it. whicb they had provided for the wants of the company. Mr. Thos; Norman seconded the motion, speaking in eulogistic terra of the host and hostess. The motion was carried with cheers, three times repeated, and Mr. Sanderson responded. Be re- marked that it had given him great pleasure to entertanf' them that day, and he should be glad to see the Runcero people as often as they liked to pay him a visit. Mr. Shasv' the seamen's missionary, proposed a vote of thanks to Cal): tam n Clarke and to Mr. Meadowcroft, agent of the 13ridge water Navigation Co., the former for so kindly lending them the use of the steamer, and the latter for the fiat. The Pre- position was seconded by Mr. Williams, and carried by ac,.: clamation. Mr. Ressendale, who accompanied the trice sponded. Mr. Norman took the opportunity to apolo.g 5; for the absence of Dr. Steele, the president, who was detan'eut, in Manchester in connection with a law suit, which no deoftyt was also the cause of other gentlemen staying awaY• liberty now to explore the beauties of the nelghbourlwe'eer the members of the party dispersed to seek pleasure e'"e, their own manner, the majority, however, finding their W. to the ancient church in the village. It was full of inte.reed to those for whom antiquities had a charm, as it contan? several monuments of great antiquity and curious benefaci tion tables; while the ascent of the tower seemed to aff°,he a little pleasurable excitement. About half-past seven j , return journey was commenced. &rigs and recitatioeof given by several ladies and gentlemen, and the singhlEso hymns, passed the time pleasantly until Weston Point reached about 10 o'cloek, when heavy rain was falliog. eto, weather, however, up to this point had been beautifully le,„. and under the conductorship of Mr. Fred Norman and r° Shaw, the trip was very successful.

ELECTION OF O')MI\IISSIONES. SINGULAR TERMINATION. The annual election of three members of the Newton Improvement Commissioners in place of the three who retire by rotation took place on Wednesday last. As will be within the recollection of our readers, the three retiring members were Messrs. George McCorquodale, James E. Pardey, and Thos. G. Gillespie. A determined attempt was, made by a section of the ratepayers to secure what they considered to be a better representation of their interests on the Board, and three new candidates appeared in the field. With the nomination of the three— retiring members, six per- sons thus sought the favour of the ratepayers. The new candidates were Benjamin Walker, out of business; Benja- min Corlett, tobacconist; and George Appleton, publican. It was understood that they were proposed at the suggestion of the " Ratepayers' Association," that the only one who was considered to have any chance of success was Mr. Appleton. As the day for the election drew near considerable interest was manifested as to the result, and this was increased by the withdrawal of Mr. Walker from the contest, who took that action on Saturday last. It was expected that Mr. Appleton would make a "tough fight" in the battle, but the centest came to a singular conclusion, which no doubt interfered very much with his schemes of success. As all the other candidates had decided to com- pete for the three seats, a poll of the ratepayers was un- avoidable. The polling was fixed to commence at nine o'clock in the morning and to remain open until four o'clock in the afternoon, the only voting place in the district being I at the Town Hall, Newton. Each of the ratepayers bad the privilege of voting for three candi- dates, and the majority of those who had an opportunity of exercising that privilege recorded their votes in favour of old members, who were re-elected by large majorities. The polling for the first two hours was pretty brisk, but not unusually so. Up to eleven o'clock the " business " gradually slackened, and as an hour—from five minutes past eleven to five minutes past twelve—inter- vened without a single vote being recorded the Returning Officer (Mr. W. F. Gooch, chairman of the Board) made an order for the closing of the poll. This was done in accordance with the law, and on the votes being counted, it was found that the result was as follows : George MeCorroodale 162 James B Parcley Thomas Gillespie 154 George Appleton Benjamin Corbett Benjamin Walker (withdrawn) Thusthe three returning members were re-elected. The closing of the poll at that hour caused some feeling among a number of the ratepayers, especially those who had to come from a distance to record their votes. A large num- ber of the persons resident in Earrestown' Sic., entitled to exercise the right conferred upon them by the law, were unable to do so owing to the sudden closing of the contest, and much disippointment was caused thereby. Suggestions have been made that in future there should be three polling stations—one at Newton, a second at Earlestown, and a third at the Vulcan, but as it was explained at the annual meeting of the ratepayers held at Newton on Wednesday last (and a report of which appears elsewhere), the Commissioners have not the power to accede to the suggestions, though, if they could be adopted, would prove of much convenience and benefit to the large number of workingmen resident in the district.
